theorem actual_tie_free_joint_exchangeability_gives_every_rank_cdf
    (n : ℕ) (law : Measure (Fin (n+1) → ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]
    (hex : exchangeable law) (hties : ∀ᵐ scores ∂law, Function.Injective scores)
    (test : Fin (n+1)) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) :
    law.real {scores | rankNat scores test < k} = (k : ℝ)/(n+1) := by
  classical
  let top : Fin (n+1) := ⟨k,by omega⟩
  let ranks : Finset (Fin (n+1)) := Finset.Iio top
  have he : {scores | rankNat scores test < k} =
      ⋃ r ∈ ranks, rankEvent test r := by
    ext scores
    constructor
    · intro hs
      refine Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨rankFin scores test,Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨?_,?_⟩⟩
      · simpa [ranks,top,Fin.lt_def,rankFin] using hs
      · rfl
    · intro hs
      obtain ⟨r,hs⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp hs
      obtain ⟨hr,he⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp hs
      have hlt : r.val < k := by simpa [ranks,top,Fin.lt_def] using hr
      change rankNat scores test = r.val at he
      change rankNat scores test < k
      rw [he]
      exact hlt
  have hd : Set.PairwiseDisjoint (↑ranks) (rankEvent test) := by
    intro r hr s hs hne
    apply Set.disjoint_left.mpr
    intro scores h1 h2
    apply hne
    apply Fin.ext
    change rankNat scores test = r.val at h1
    change rankNat scores test = s.val at h2
    exact h1.symm.trans h2
  rw [he,measureReal_biUnion_finset hd (fun r _ => actual_rank_event_measurable test r)]
  simp_rw [actual_tie_free_exchangeable_rank_is_uniform law hex hties test]
  simp [ranks,top,Fin.card_Iio,div_eq_mul_inv]

theorem actual_calibration_success_is_the_strict_rank_cdf
    {n : ℕ} (scores : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (test : Fin (n+1)) (k : ℕ) :
    (scores test : EReal) ≤ calibrationThreshold scores test k ↔
      rankNat scores test < k := by
  rw [←not_lt,calibration_failure_iff,not_le]
  rfl

theorem actual_tie_free_split_calibration_coverage_is_exact
    (n : ℕ) (law : Measure (Fin (n+1) → ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]
    (hex : exchangeable law) (hties : ∀ᵐ scores ∂law,Function.Injective scores)
    (test : Fin (n+1)) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) :
    law.real {scores | (scores test : EReal) ≤ calibrationThreshold scores test k} =
      (k : ℝ)/(n+1) := by
  have he : {scores | (scores test : EReal) ≤ calibrationThreshold scores test k} =
      {scores | rankNat scores test < k} := by
    ext scores
    exact actual_calibration_success_is_the_strict_rank_cdf scores test k
  rw [he]
  exact actual_tie_free_joint_exchangeability_gives_every_rank_cdf n law hex hties test k hk

theorem actual_ceiling_rank_has_the_literal_two_sided_coverage_arithmetic
    (n : ℕ) (alpha : ℝ) (ha : alpha ≤ 1) :
    1-alpha ≤ (conformalRank n alpha : ℝ)/(n+1) ∧
      (conformalRank n alpha : ℝ)/(n+1) < 1-alpha+1/(n+1) := by
  have hp : (0 : ℝ)<n+1 := by positivity
  simp only [conformalRank,Nat.cast_add,Nat.cast_one]
  have hlo := Nat.le_ceil (((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)*(1-alpha))
  have hhi := Nat.ceil_lt_add_one (mul_nonneg (show (0 : ℝ)≤((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ) by positivity) (sub_nonneg.mpr ha))
  simp only [Nat.cast_add,Nat.cast_one] at hlo hhi
  constructor
  · apply (le_div_iff₀ hp).mpr
    change (1-alpha)*(n+1) ≤ (Nat.ceil ((n+1 : ℝ)*(1-alpha)) : ℝ)
    nlinarith
  · apply (div_lt_iff₀ hp).mpr
    have hdiv : (1/(n+1 : ℝ))*(n+1)=1 := by field_simp [hp.ne']
    change (Nat.ceil ((n+1 : ℝ)*(1-alpha)) : ℝ)<(1-alpha+1/(n+1))*(n+1)
    nlinarith

theorem actual_nine_and_ten_calibration_ranks_and_exact_ratios :
    conformalRank 9 (1/10)=9 ∧ conformalRank 10 (1/10)=10 ∧
      (9 : ℝ)/10=9/10 ∧ (10 : ℝ)/11>9/10 ∧
      |(10 : ℝ)/11-909/1000| < 1/1000 := by
  norm_num [conformalRank,Nat.ceil_eq_iff]



theorem actual_nine_calibration_threshold_is_an_attained_real_maximum
    (scores : Fin 10 → ℝ) (test : Fin 10) :
    ∃ i : Fin 10, i ≠ test ∧
      IsGreatest (scores '' {j | j ≠ test}) (scores i) ∧
      calibrationThreshold scores test 9 = (scores i : EReal) := by
  classical
  letI : DecidableEq (Fin 10) := Classical.decEq (Fin 10)
  let s : Finset (Fin 10) := Finset.univ.erase test
  have hc : s.card = 9 := by simp [s]
  have hn : s.Nonempty := Finset.card_pos.mp (by omega)
  obtain ⟨i,hi,hm⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup s hn (fun j => (scores j : EReal))
  have hit : i ≠ test := (Finset.mem_erase.mp hi).1
  refine ⟨i,hit,⟨⟨i,hit,rfl⟩,?_⟩,?_⟩
  · rintro y ⟨j,hjt,rfl⟩
    have hj : j ∈ s := Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hjt,Finset.mem_univ _⟩
    have hle := Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => (scores j : EReal)) hj
    rw [hm] at hle
    exact EReal.coe_le_coe_iff.mp hle
  · unfold calibrationThreshold
    change ((Finset.univ.erase test).powersetCard 9).inf
      (fun subset => subset.sup (fun j => (scores j : EReal))) = (scores i : EReal)
    rw [←hc,Finset.powersetCard_self,Finset.inf_singleton]
    exact hm

theorem actual_tie_free_split_calibration_has_both_literal_coverage_bounds
    (n : ℕ) (law : Measure (Fin (n+1) → ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]
    (hex : exchangeable law) (hties : ∀ᵐ scores ∂law,Function.Injective scores)
    (test : Fin (n+1)) (alpha : ℝ) (ha : alpha ≤ 1)
    (hk : conformalRank n alpha ≤ n) :
    1-alpha ≤ law.real {scores | (scores test : EReal) ≤
      calibrationThreshold scores test (conformalRank n alpha)} ∧
    law.real {scores | (scores test : EReal) ≤
      calibrationThreshold scores test (conformalRank n alpha)} <
        1-alpha+1/(n+1) := by
  rw [actual_tie_free_split_calibration_coverage_is_exact n law hex hties test
    (conformalRank n alpha) hk]
  exact actual_ceiling_rank_has_the_literal_two_sided_coverage_arithmetic n alpha ha

theorem actual_constant_nine_calibration_scores_are_always_covered_and_break_the_strict_upper
    (law : Measure (Fin 10 → ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure law] (test : Fin 10) :
    law.real {scores | ((0 : ℝ) : EReal) ≤
      calibrationThreshold (fun _ : Fin 10 => (0 : ℝ)) test 9} = 1 ∧
    ¬ (law.real {scores | ((0 : ℝ) : EReal) ≤
      calibrationThreshold (fun _ : Fin 10 => (0 : ℝ)) test 9} <
        1-(1/10 : ℝ)+1/10) := by
  obtain ⟨i,hi,hgreat,hthreshold⟩ :=
    actual_nine_calibration_threshold_is_an_attained_real_maximum (fun _ => 0) test
  have he : calibrationThreshold (fun _ : Fin 10 => (0 : ℝ)) test 9 = (0 : ℝ) := by
    simpa using hthreshold
  simp [he]

Exercise 15.3 — Prove the split-conformal coverage bound
      
      
        Let $s_1,\dots,s_n,s_{n+1}$ be exchangeable, almost surely distinct scores ($s_{n+1}$ is the test score) and $\hat q=s_{(k)}$ with $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil\le n$. (a) Prove $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)=k/(n+1)$. (b) Deduce $1-\alpha\le\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)\lt1-\alpha+\tfrac1{n+1}$. (c) For $n=9$, $\alpha=0.1$, what is $\hat q$ and what is the exact coverage? (d) Why does the lower bound survive ties while the upper bound may not?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) Let $\rho$ be the rank of $s_{n+1}$ among the $n+1$ scores. Exchangeability means the joint law is invariant under permutations, so $\mathbb P(\rho=r)$ is the same for every $r\in\{1,\dots,n+1\}$, hence $1/(n+1)$. The event $s_{n+1}\le s_{(k)}$ (the $k$-th smallest of the other $n$ scores) means that at most $k-1$ of the others are smaller than $s_{n+1}$, i.e. $\rho\le k$. Therefore $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)=\mathbb P(\rho\le k)=k/(n+1)$.
            (b) By definition of the ceiling, $(n+1)(1-\alpha)\le k\lt(n+1)(1-\alpha)+1$; divide by $n+1$.
            (c) $k=\lceil 10\cdot0.9\rceil=9$: $\hat q$ is the largest calibration score and the coverage is exactly $9/10=0.9$ (the prediction set is as tight as the guarantee allows, but only because $(n+1)(1-\alpha)$ is an integer; for $n=10$ one gets $k=\lceil9.9\rceil=10$ and coverage $10/11\approx0.909$).
            (d) With ties, attach an independent uniform tie-breaker $U_i$ to every score and order the pairs $(s_i,U_i)$ lexicographically. The pairs are exchangeable and almost surely distinct, so by (a) the rank $\rho$ of the test pair satisfies $\mathbb P(\rho\le k)=k/(n+1)$. If $\rho\le k$, at most $k-1$ calibration pairs precede the test pair, so at most $k-1$ calibration scores are strictly smaller than $s_{n+1}$ and $s_{n+1}\le s_{(k)}=\hat q$. Hence $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)\ge k/(n+1)$: the lower bound is safe. The converse fails: a test score tied with $s_{(k)}$ is covered even when its tie-breaker ranks it after position $k$, and the probability can exceed $k/(n+1)$ by the mass of ties at $s_{(k)}$; the upper bound $1-\alpha+\tfrac1{n+1}$ therefore requires a continuous score distribution or randomised tie-breaking in the prediction set itself. In the extreme case of a constant score, $\mathcal C$ always contains everything and coverage is 1.

Review if needed: Primer C: binomial tails and exchangeability; this module's relevant section.

Hint

For $d=3$, sum the binomial probabilities for $i=0,1,2$. The outer randomness is the design sample.

Worked solution

Step 1. The explicit rule gives $N\ge20(\ln20+3)\approx119.91465$, so $N=120$ suffices.

Step 2. The exact tail is $S_N=0.9^N+N(0.1)0.9^{N-1}+\binom N2(0.1)^2 0.9^{N-2}$. It gives $S_{60}\approx0.05304508\gt0.05$ and $S_{61}\approx0.04911828\le0.05$. The tail decreases with $N$, so $61$ is the smallest admissible count.

Step 3. The theorem states that, with probability at least $0.95$ over the sampled design constraints, the returned solution has population violation probability at most $0.1$. It does not prove zero violation for every uncertainty realization; convexity, feasibility/solution assumptions and matching i.i.d. deployment sampling remain necessary.

Hard 4 — Conditioning on planner feasibility changes the bound

A conformal planning argument proves $\mathbb P(\text{feasible and unsafe})\le0.04$, while $\mathbb P(\text{feasible})=0.5$. What upper bound follows on failure conditional on feasibility? Does the argument prove unconditional safety at least $0.96$ if behavior on infeasible runs is unspecified?

Review if needed: Primer C: conditional probability; this module's relevant section.

Hint

Use the definition of conditional probability; the event inclusion controls only one part of all runs.

Worked solution

Step 1. $\mathbb P(\text{unsafe}\mid\text{feasible})=\mathbb P(\text{unsafe and feasible})/0.5\le0.04/0.5=0.08$. Thus the conditional safety lower bound from these facts is $0.92$.

Step 2. Infeasible runs have probability $0.5$ and may all be unsafe. The given facts alone therefore permit unconditional unsafe probability as high as $0.5+0.04=0.54$, yielding only the lower bound $0.46$ on safety.

Step 3. To obtain the intended unconditional safety statement, prove almost-sure feasibility or add a certified safe fallback for infeasible cases. Simply discarding infeasible runs changes the probability space and does not preserve the original $0.96$ claim.

Original research exercises

Continue here when the core calculations and the certificate assumptions are clear. Use the graded questions above as a warm-up; the original derivations below remain available in full.

Exercise 15.1 — Derive the IBP affine rule and exhibit its joint looseness

(a) Let $a\in[\underline a,\overline a]$ and $z=Wa+b$. Derive the interval $[\underline z,\overline z]$ produced by IBP and show that each coordinate bound is attained. (b) For $W=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $b=0$ and $a\in[-1,1]^2$, describe the true image $\{Wa\}$ and find a point of the IBP box that is not in it.

Show answer

(a) Write $a=\mu+\delta$ with $\mu=\tfrac12(\overline a+\underline a)$, $|\delta_j|\le r_j=\tfrac12(\overline a_j-\underline a_j)$. Then $z_i=W_{i,:}\mu+b_i+W_{i,:}\delta$ and $|W_{i,:}\delta|\le\sum_j|W_{ij}||\delta_j|\le\sum_j|W_{ij}|r_j=(|W|r)_i$ (triangle inequality, then $|\delta_j|\le r_j$). So $\underline z=W\mu+b-|W|r$, $\overline z=W\mu+b+|W|r$. Choosing $\delta_j=r_j\,\mathrm{sign}(W_{ij})$ makes every term $|W_{ij}|r_j$ and this $\delta$ is feasible, so $\overline z_i$ is attained; $\delta_j=-r_j\,\mathrm{sign}(W_{ij})$ attains $\underline z_i$.

(b) $\mu=0$, $r=(1,1)$, $|W|r=(2,2)$: IBP gives $z\in[-2,2]^2$. The true image is the set of $(a_1+a_2,\,a_1-a_2)$ with $|a_i|\le1$, a square rotated by $45^\circ$ with vertices $(\pm2,0)$ and $(0,\pm2)$ (equivalently $|z_1|+|z_2|\le 2$). The IBP corner $(2,2)$ would need $a_1+a_2=2$ and $a_1-a_2=2$, i.e. $a_1=2$, which is infeasible. The box has area 16, the image has area 8: IBP doubles the area in a single layer, and the next layer may combine $z_1=2$ with $z_2=2$ as if both were reachable at once.

Exercise 15.2 — CROWN bounds for the walkthrough network at other radii

Repeat the walkthrough for the same network and $x_0=(1,1)$ with (a) $\varepsilon=0.5$ and (b) $\varepsilon=1.5$: give the pre-activation bounds, the neuron statuses, the IBP interval, the adaptive-CROWN interval, the α-CROWN lower bound and the exact range. Check with Panel A.

Show answer

(a) $\varepsilon=0.5$: $r=|W|(0.5,0.5)^{\top}=(1,1.5)$, so $z_1\in[2,4]$, $z_2\in[0.5,3.5]$: both neurons stable active. IBP: $a_1\in[2,4]$, $a_2\in[0.5,3.5]$, $f\in[-8+1,\,-4+7]=[-7,3]$. CROWN needs no relaxation: $f=-2z_1+2z_2=-4x_1+2x_2$ exactly, $\Omega=(-4,2)$, $\Omega x_0=-2$, $\|\Omega\|_1=6$, so $f\in[-2-3,\,-2+3]=[-5,1]$, which is also the exact range (attained at $(1.5,0.5)$ and $(0.5,1.5)$). Lesson: IBP is loose even without any unstable neuron, purely through the joint-box effect of Exercise 15.1; CROWN is exact for an affine function.

(b) $\varepsilon=1.5$: $r=(3,4.5)$, $z_1\in[0,6]$ (stable active, $l_1=0$), $z_2\in[-2.5,6.5]$ (unstable). IBP: $a_1\in[0,6]$, $a_2\in[0,6.5]$, $f\in[-12,13]$. Adaptive CROWN: $u_2=6.5\ge|l_2|$ so $\alpha=1$; lower line $z_2$, upper chord $\tfrac{6.5}{9}(z_2+2.5)$. Lower bound: $f\ge-2z_1+2\alpha z_2$ with $\Omega=(-2-2\alpha,\,-2+4\alpha)$, $c=-2+2\alpha$, giving $\gamma^L(\alpha)=-6+4\alpha-1.5\,(2+2\alpha+|4\alpha-2|)=-9+\alpha-1.5|4\alpha-2|$: $\gamma^L(1)=-11$ (CROWN), $\gamma^L(0)=-12$ (= IBP), maximum $\gamma^L(\tfrac12)=-8.5$ (α-CROWN). Upper bound: $\Lambda=(-\tfrac{31}{9},\tfrac89)$, $c_U=\tfrac{55}{18}$, $\Lambda x_0+c_U=\tfrac12$, $\gamma^U=\tfrac12+1.5\cdot\tfrac{39}{9}=7$. Exact: on $\{z_2\ge0\}$, $f=-4x_1+2x_2$ with minimum $-8.5$ at the kink point $(2.5,0.75)$ and maximum $7$ at $(-0.5,2.5)$; on $\{z_2\le0\}$, $f=-2x_1-2x_2-2\ge-8.5$. So exact $=[-8.5,7]$, α-CROWN $=[-8.5,7]$, CROWN $=[-11,7]$, IBP $=[-12,13]$.

Exercise 15.3 — Prove the split-conformal coverage bound

Let $s_1,\dots,s_n,s_{n+1}$ be exchangeable, almost surely distinct scores ($s_{n+1}$ is the test score) and $\hat q=s_{(k)}$ with $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil\le n$. (c) For $n=9$, $\alpha=0.1$, what is $\hat q$ and what is the exact coverage? (d) Why does the lower bound survive ties while the upper bound may not?

Show answer

(a) Let $\rho$ be the rank of $s_{n+1}$ among the $n+1$ scores. Exchangeability means the joint law is invariant under permutations, so $\mathbb P(\rho=r)$ is the same for every $r\in\{1,\dots,n+1\}$, hence $1/(n+1)$. The event $s_{n+1}\le s_{(k)}$ (the $k$-th smallest of the other $n$ scores) means that at most $k-1$ of the others are smaller than $s_{n+1}$, i.e. $\rho\le k$. Therefore $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)=\mathbb P(\rho\le k)=k/(n+1)$.

(b) By definition of the ceiling, $(n+1)(1-\alpha)\le k\lt(n+1)(1-\alpha)+1$; divide by $n+1$.

(c) $k=\lceil 10\cdot0.9\rceil=9$: $\hat q$ is the largest calibration score and the coverage is exactly $9/10=0.9$ (the prediction set is as tight as the guarantee allows, but only because $(n+1)(1-\alpha)$ is an integer; for $n=10$ one gets $k=\lceil9.9\rceil=10$ and coverage $10/11\approx0.909$).

(d) With ties, attach an independent uniform tie-breaker $U_i$ to every score and order the pairs $(s_i,U_i)$ lexicographically. The pairs are exchangeable and almost surely distinct, so by (a) the rank $\rho$ of the test pair satisfies $\mathbb P(\rho\le k)=k/(n+1)$. If $\rho\le k$, at most $k-1$ calibration pairs precede the test pair, so at most $k-1$ calibration scores are strictly smaller than $s_{n+1}$ and $s_{n+1}\le s_{(k)}=\hat q$. Hence $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)\ge k/(n+1)$: the lower bound is safe. The converse fails: a test score tied with $s_{(k)}$ is covered even when its tie-breaker ranks it after position $k$, and the probability can exceed $k/(n+1)$ by the mass of ties at $s_{(k)}$; the upper bound $1-\alpha+\tfrac1{n+1}$ therefore requires a continuous score distribution or randomised tie-breaking in the prediction set itself. import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
namespace SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedConformalRanks
open Set Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators Topology

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- Zero-based strict rank of an actual coordinate among all finite scores. -/
def rankNat (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores index)).card

theorem actual_rank_is_less_than_sample_size (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) :
    rankNat scores index < n := by
  have hs : Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores index) ⊂ Finset.univ := by
    refine ⟨Finset.filter_subset _ _,?_⟩
    intro hall
    have h := hall (Finset.mem_univ index)
    simp at h
  simpa [rankNat] using Finset.card_lt_card hs

def rankFin (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) : Fin n :=
  ⟨rankNat scores index,actual_rank_is_less_than_sample_size scores index⟩

theorem actual_strict_score_order_gives_strict_rank_order
    (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (first second : Fin n) (h : scores first < scores second) :
    rankNat scores first < rankNat scores second := by
  have hs : Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores first) ⊂
      Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores second) := by
    constructor
    · intro j hj
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _,
        lt_trans (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2 h⟩
    · intro hall
      have hi := hall (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ first,h⟩)
      simp at hi
  exact Finset.card_lt_card hs

theorem actual_distinct_scores_have_bijective_ranks (scores : Fin n → ℝ)
    (h : Function.Injective scores) : Function.Bijective (rankFin scores) := by
  have hi : Function.Injective (rankFin scores) := by
    intro i j he
    have hv : rankNat scores i=rankNat scores j := congrArg Fin.val he
    by_contra hij
    have hs : scores i ≠ scores j := fun he => hij (h he)
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hs with hs|hs
    · exact (ne_of_lt (actual_strict_score_order_gives_strict_rank_order scores i j hs)) hv
    · exact (ne_of_lt (actual_strict_score_order_gives_strict_rank_order scores j i hs)) hv.symm
  exact ⟨hi,(Finite.injective_iff_surjective).mp hi⟩

theorem actual_each_rank_occurs_exactly_once (scores : Fin n → ℝ)
    (h : Function.Injective scores) (rank : Fin n) :
    (∑ i : Fin n,if rankNat scores i=rank.val then (1:ℝ) else 0)=1 := by
  obtain ⟨index,hi⟩ := (actual_distinct_scores_have_bijective_ranks scores h).2 rank
  have he : ∀ i : Fin n,rankNat scores i=rank.val ↔ i=index := by
    intro i
    constructor
    · intro ht
      apply (actual_distinct_scores_have_bijective_ranks scores h).1
      apply Fin.ext
      exact ht.trans (congrArg Fin.val hi).symm
    · intro ht
      subst i
      exact congrArg Fin.val hi
  simp_rw [he]
  simp

theorem actual_rank_is_measurable (index : Fin n) :
    Measurable (fun scores : Fin n → ℝ => rankNat scores index) := by
  have he : (fun scores : Fin n → ℝ => rankNat scores index)=
      (fun scores => ∑ j : Fin n,if scores j<scores index then (1:ℕ) else 0) := by
    funext scores
    simp [rankNat]
  rw [he]
  exact Finset.measurable_fun_sum Finset.univ (fun j _ =>
    Measurable.ite (measurableSet_lt (measurable_pi_apply j) (measurable_pi_apply index))
      measurable_const measurable_const)

def permutedScores (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (scores : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin n → ℝ :=
  fun i => scores (permutation i)

theorem actual_permuted_scores_are_measurable (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    Measurable (permutedScores permutation) := by
  exact Measurable.of_eval (fun i => measurable_pi_apply (permutation i))

theorem actual_relabeling_preserves_the_corresponding_rank
    (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) :
    rankNat (permutedScores permutation scores) index=rankNat scores (permutation index) := by
  have hl : rankNat (permutedScores permutation scores) index=
      ∑ j : Fin n,if scores (permutation j)<scores (permutation index) then (1:ℕ) else 0 := by
    simp [rankNat,permutedScores]
    rfl
  rw [hl]
  calc
    _ = ∑ j : Fin n,if scores j<scores (permutation index) then (1:ℕ) else 0 :=
      Fintype.sum_equiv permutation _ _ (fun _ => rfl)
    _ = _ := by simp [rankNat]

def rankEvent (index : Fin n) (rank : Fin n) : Set (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  {scores | rankNat scores index=rank.val}

theorem actual_rank_event_measurable (index rank : Fin n) : MeasurableSet (rankEvent index rank) :=
  (actual_rank_is_measurable index) (measurableSet_singleton rank.val)

/-- Exchangeability is invariance of the genuine joint score law under every
coordinate permutation, rather than an assumed uniform-rank conclusion. -/
def exchangeable (law : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),law.map (permutedScores permutation)=law

theorem actual_exchangeability_gives_equal_coordinate_rank_probabilities
    (law : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) (h : exchangeable law) (first second rank : Fin n) :
    law.real (rankEvent first rank)=law.real (rankEvent second rank) := by
  have hm := actual_permuted_scores_are_measurable (Equiv.swap first second)
  rw [←h (Equiv.swap first second),map_measureReal_apply hm (actual_rank_event_measurable first rank)]
  have he : permutedScores (Equiv.swap first second) ⁻¹' rankEvent first rank=rankEvent second rank := by
    ext scores
    simp only [Set.mem_preimage,rankEvent,Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
    rw [actual_relabeling_preserves_the_corresponding_rank,Equiv.swap_apply_left]
  rw [he,h (Equiv.swap first second)]

theorem actual_tie_free_exchangeable_rank_is_uniform
    (law : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]
    (hex : exchangeable law) (hties : ∀ᵐ scores ∂law,Function.Injective scores)
    (index rank : Fin n) : law.real (rankEvent index rank)=1/(n:ℝ) := by
  have hs : ∑ i : Fin n,law.real (rankEvent i rank)=1 := by
    calc
      _ = ∑ i : Fin n,∫ scores,(rankEvent i rank).indicator (fun _ => (1:ℝ)) scores ∂law := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro i hi
        symm
        simpa only [smul_eq_mul,mul_one] using
          integral_indicator_const (1:ℝ) (actual_rank_event_measurable i rank)
      _ = ∫ scores,∑ i : Fin n,(rankEvent i rank).indicator (fun _ => (1:ℝ)) scores ∂law := by
        symm
        apply integral_finsetSum
        intro i hi
        exact (integrable_const (1:ℝ)).indicator (actual_rank_event_measurable i rank)
      _ = ∫ _scores,1 ∂law := by
        apply integral_congr_ae
        filter_upwards [hties] with scores hscore
        calc
          _ = ∑ i : Fin n,if rankNat scores i=rank.val then (1:ℝ) else 0 := by
            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
            intro i hi
            by_cases h : rankNat scores i=rank.val <;> simp [rankEvent,Set.indicator,h]
          _ = 1 := actual_each_rank_occurs_exactly_once scores hscore rank
      _ = 1 := by simp
  have he : ∑ i : Fin n,law.real (rankEvent i rank)=
      (n:ℝ)*law.real (rankEvent index rank) := by
    simp_rw [actual_exchangeability_gives_equal_coordinate_rank_probabilities law hex _ index rank]
    simp
  rw [he] at hs
  have hn : (n:ℝ)≠0 := by
    have hp : 0<n := Nat.zero_lt_of_lt index.isLt
    exact_mod_cast hp.ne'
  apply (eq_div_iff hn).mpr
  nlinarith

end SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedConformalRanks

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteConformal

def strictRank {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (scores : ι → ℝ) (i : ι) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter fun j => scores j < scores i).card

def badIndices {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (scores : ι → ℝ) (rank : ℕ) : Finset ι :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun i => rank ≤ strictRank scores i

theorem strictRank_permute {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (scores : ι → ℝ) (p : Equiv.Perm ι) (i : ι) :
    strictRank (fun j => scores (p j)) i = strictRank scores (p i) := by

  unfold strictRank
  apply Finset.card_bij (fun j _ => p j)
  · intro j hj
    simpa only [Finset.mem_filter,Finset.mem_univ,true_and] using hj
  · intro a _ b _ h
    exact p.injective h
  · intro b hb
    refine ⟨p.symm b,?_,by simp⟩
    simpa only [Finset.mem_filter,Finset.mem_univ,true_and,p.apply_symm_apply] using hb

    have hk : rank ≤ strictRank scores i := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2

  · have hz := Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.mp he
    simp [hz]

    Measurable (fun scores : ι → ℝ => strictRank scores i) := by
  classical
  unfold strictRank
  simp only [Finset.card_eq_sum_ones,Finset.sum_filter]
  apply Finset.measurable_sum
  intro j _
  exact Measurable.ite (measurableSet_lt (measurable_pi_apply j) (measurable_pi_apply i))
    measurable_const measurable_const

  measurableSet_le measurable_const (measurable_strictRank i)

    (μ : Measure Ω) (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ)
    (hex : ∀ p : Equiv.Perm ι,

    (p : Equiv.Perm ι) (i : ι) (rank : ℕ) :

  simpa only [preimage_ofPred_eq,strictRank_permute] using h

    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores) (rank : ℕ) (i : ι) :

    Finset.sum_filter,Nat.cast_ite,Nat.cast_one,Nat.cast_zero,Set.indicator,mem_ofPred_eq]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  by_cases h : rank ≤ strictRank (scores ω) i <;> simp only [h,if_true,if_false]

    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

    simpa only [smul_eq_mul,mul_one] using

      intro ω

        ((Fintype.card ι-rank : ℕ) : ℝ)
      rw [bad_indicator_count]

    _ = _ := by simp

theorem exchangeable_rank_failure_bound {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)
    (hex : ∀ p : Equiv.Perm ι,
      IdentDistrib (fun ω i => scores ω (p i)) scores μ μ)
    (rank : ℕ) (i : ι) :

    (scores : ι → ℝ) (test : ι) (rank : ℕ) : EReal := by

    obtain ⟨subset,hsub,hcard⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq h
    refine ⟨subset,Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨?_,hcard⟩,?_⟩
    · intro j hj
      have hjlt := (Finset.mem_filter.mp (hsub hj)).2
      have hne : j ≠ test := by intro he;rw [he] at hjlt;exact (lt_irrefl _) hjlt
      exact Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hne,Finset.mem_univ j⟩
    · apply (Finset.sup_lt_iff (EReal.bot_lt_coe _)).mpr
      intro j hj
      exact EReal.coe_lt_coe_iff.mpr ((Finset.mem_filter.mp (hsub hj)).2)

    (scores : ι → ℝ) (test : ι) (rank : ℕ) (h : Fintype.card ι-1 < rank) :

    exact h

    [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)
    (hex : ∀ p : Equiv.Perm ι,

    (rank : ℕ) (test : ι) :

theorem conformal_success_bound {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)

  Nat.ceil (((sampleCount+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)*(1-alpha))

theorem conformalRank_le (n : ℕ) (alpha : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ alpha) :
    conformalRank n alpha ≤ n+1 := by
  unfold conformalRank

  have hn : (0 : ℝ) ≤ n+1 := by positivity

    1-alpha ≤ 1-(((n+1-conformalRank n alpha : ℕ) : ℝ)/((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) := by
  have hle := conformalRank_le n alpha ha
  have hceil := Nat.le_ceil (((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)*(1-alpha))

    (n : ℕ) (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)

noncomputable section
namespace SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedConformalRanks
open Set Filter MeasureTheory

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- Zero-based strict rank of an actual coordinate among all finite scores. -/
def rankNat (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores index)).card

theorem actual_rank_is_less_than_sample_size (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) :
    rankNat scores index < n := by
  have hs : Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores index) ⊂ Finset.univ := by
    refine ⟨Finset.filter_subset _ _,?_⟩
    intro hall
    have h := hall (Finset.mem_univ index)
    simp at h
  simpa [rankNat] using Finset.card_lt_card hs

def rankFin (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) : Fin n :=
  ⟨rankNat scores index,actual_rank_is_less_than_sample_size scores index⟩

theorem actual_strict_score_order_gives_strict_rank_order
    (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (first second : Fin n) (h : scores first < scores second) :
    rankNat scores first < rankNat scores second := by
  have hs : Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores first) ⊂
      Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores second) := by
    constructor
    · intro j hj
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _,
        lt_trans (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2 h⟩
    · intro hall
      have hi := hall (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ first,h⟩)
      simp at hi
  exact Finset.card_lt_card hs

theorem actual_distinct_scores_have_bijective_ranks (scores : Fin n → ℝ)
    (h : Function.Injective scores) : Function.Bijective (rankFin scores) := by
  have hi : Function.Injective (rankFin scores) := by
    intro i j he
    have hv : rankNat scores i=rankNat scores j := congrArg Fin.val he
    by_contra hij
    have hs : scores i ≠ scores j := fun he => hij (h he)
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hs with hs|hs
    · exact (ne_of_lt (actual_strict_score_order_gives_strict_rank_order scores i j hs)) hv
    · exact (ne_of_lt (actual_strict_score_order_gives_strict_rank_order scores j i hs)) hv.symm
  exact ⟨hi,(Finite.injective_iff_surjective).mp hi⟩

theorem actual_each_rank_occurs_exactly_once (scores : Fin n → ℝ)
    (h : Function.Injective scores) (rank : Fin n) :
    (∑ i : Fin n,if rankNat scores i=rank.val then (1:ℝ) else 0)=1 := by
  obtain ⟨index,hi⟩ := (actual_distinct_scores_have_bijective_ranks scores h).2 rank
  have he : ∀ i : Fin n,rankNat scores i=rank.val ↔ i=index := by
    intro i
    constructor
    · intro ht
      apply (actual_distinct_scores_have_bijective_ranks scores h).1
      apply Fin.ext
      exact ht.trans (congrArg Fin.val hi).symm
    · intro ht
      subst i
      exact congrArg Fin.val hi
  simp_rw [he]
  simp

theorem actual_rank_is_measurable (index : Fin n) :
    Measurable (fun scores : Fin n → ℝ => rankNat scores index) := by
  have he : (fun scores : Fin n → ℝ => rankNat scores index)=
      (fun scores => ∑ j : Fin n,if scores j<scores index then (1:ℕ) else 0) := by
    funext scores
    simp [rankNat]
  rw [he]
  exact Finset.measurable_fun_sum Finset.univ (fun j _ =>
    Measurable.ite (measurableSet_lt (measurable_pi_apply j) (measurable_pi_apply index))
      measurable_const measurable_const)

def permutedScores (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (scores : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin n → ℝ :=
  fun i => scores (permutation i)

theorem actual_permuted_scores_are_measurable (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    Measurable (permutedScores permutation) := by
  exact Measurable.of_eval (fun i => measurable_pi_apply (permutation i))

theorem actual_relabeling_preserves_the_corresponding_rank
    (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) :
    rankNat (permutedScores permutation scores) index=rankNat scores (permutation index) := by
  have hl : rankNat (permutedScores permutation scores) index=
      ∑ j : Fin n,if scores (permutation j)<scores (permutation index) then (1:ℕ) else 0 := by
    simp [rankNat,permutedScores]
    rfl
  rw [hl]

      Fintype.sum_equiv permutation _ _ (fun _ => rfl)
    _ = _ := by simp [rankNat]

def rankEvent (index : Fin n) (rank : Fin n) : Set (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  {scores | rankNat scores index=rank.val}

theorem actual_rank_event_measurable (index rank : Fin n) : MeasurableSet (rankEvent index rank) :=
  (actual_rank_is_measurable index) (measurableSet_singleton rank.val)

/-- Exchangeability is invariance of the genuine joint score law under every

def exchangeable (law : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),law.map (permutedScores permutation)=law

    (law : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) (h : exchangeable law) (first second rank : Fin n) :
    law.real (rankEvent first rank)=law.real (rankEvent second rank) := by
  have hm := actual_permuted_scores_are_measurable (Equiv.swap first second)
  rw [←h (Equiv.swap first second),map_measureReal_apply hm (actual_rank_event_measurable first rank)]
  have he : permutedScores (Equiv.swap first second) ⁻¹' rankEvent first rank=rankEvent second rank := by
    ext scores
    simp only [Set.mem_preimage,rankEvent,Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
    rw [actual_relabeling_preserves_the_corresponding_rank,Equiv.swap_apply_left]
  rw [he,h (Equiv.swap first second)]

        intro i hi

        intro i hi

        apply integral_congr_ae

            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
